doc.title: Mrs. P. Thomas Agnes Brown Interview, 1960-10-12

title: Tom Brown's written claim to have started jazz in Chicago
summary: A reading of Tom's verse claiming he started jazz in Chicago in 1915 and took the first band there, crediting his bandmates; a spelling puzzle over the 'glorified piano'.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

Jazz is a big ballahoo today. Would you like to meet the man that started jazz? He's right here in your city standing fast. You shouldn't believe a word of what you've already heard. They're busy telling lies of what they heard. Tom Brown started jazz in Chicago, even built a name for jazz. Jazz was never used to music until Tom, until Brown, I'm sorry, gave it its advance. The colored were not responsible as the great big ballahoo. It was done by the north to kid the south. The colored only played plantation and jazz as a part of swing. You can see how well it has done as they are all having fun, telling what they've done to create jazz. It was started in 1915. Don't be fooled. It wasn't until then everyone has taken copy and claiming that he's the one. The world has misunderstood the correct point of jazz. There's always room for correction for things done in the past. This is the only way I have to get back at them for something wrongfully done. It's too late to derive any benefits. It's let's put it all in song. Give the right where right belongs. I just want my public to know the truth. T.S. Tom Brown took the first band to Chicago. You can see how well it has done. Then down at the bottom, after the signature as it has, Ray did a lot to perfect this jazz. Gus variated to the strain of swing. Arnold played the glorified piano.
The Graf-A. They call it the Graf-A piano.
What does that mean? Read that. He played the Graf-A. Read it again.
I want to play the G-L-O-F-A-R-E.
That means the Graf-A the piano.
While Bill added tempo to the strain, Tom played a kind of lick here and there to add the beautiful tone. When they were all together, you had the finest jazz in the land.
Now, you read that really good.
Now, that would be wonderful. You want that on tape?
